column1: # Dated changes to laboratory testing capacity, read off the situation reports.
# WHY THIS EXISTS. Test positivity is a ratio whose denominator is decided by
# how many people get sampled, and that is a property of the response rather
# than of the epidemic. A fall in positivity means one of two very different
# things -- less virus among the people being tested, or a wider set of people
# being tested -- and the reports occasionally say outright when the second
# changed. Those statements are the only direct evidence we have for reading
# the ratio, so they are recorded here rather than left in prose nobody
# revisits, and the positivity figures mark them.
# WHAT GOES IN. Only a dated statement in a report that testing capacity
# itself changed: equipment received or installed, a laboratory opening, a
# site beginning or ceasing to analyse. NOT a change in observed volume --
# volume is measured in `data/build/series/lab_prose.csv` and inferring a
# capacity event from a jump in it would make the figure argue in a circle.
# If the reports do not say it, it does not go here.
# EVERY ROW CARRIES THE SENTENCE IT CAME FROM, in the source's own words, so
# a reader can disagree with our reading without going back to the PDF. The
# `sitrep` column is where to look if they want to anyway.
# WHAT THIS DOES NOT ESTABLISH. A recorded event is not a demonstrated cause.
# Ituri's testing rose by about two thirds between mid-July and late August
# and no report we have read states a capacity change for Ituri; the two
# events below name Nord-Kivu and Haut-Uélé, and of those only Haut-Uélé's
# volume moved. The register is evidence to reason with, not an explanation.
# COLUMNS
#   date       the report's data date, the day the statement was published
#   sitrep     the report number, so the claim can be checked against the page
#   province   the province the statement is about
#   kind       equipment_received | installation_pending | site_opened
#   summary    a short phrase for a figure label
#   quote      the source's own sentence, verbatim, French as printed
date
